title: Engineering voice agents: Latency, quality, and scale — Rishabh Bhargava, Together AI
talk_summary: Rishabh describes production voice-agent pipelines (STT→LLM→TTS) and the latency, quality, tool-calling, and scaling constraints that dominate them. He argues speech-to-speech is promising but still weak at instruction following/tool calling, so most production systems use cascaded components with guardrails, evals, and observability.

takeaways.technique: Separate tool-call schema validity from task correctness
takeaways.what_they_do: For LLM tool calling, evaluate whether the call structure is valid separately from whether the chosen action/output is correct; aim for near-100% structural validity.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the tool call structure to at least be very close to 100%
takeaways.numbers: near 100% tool-call structure validity; correctness threshold use-case dependent

takeaways.technique: Fine-tune a small model for tool calling
takeaways.what_they_do: Use use-case-specific data to fine-tune a smaller LLM so tool-calling quality rises while staying within latency/cost budget.
takeaways.evidence_quote: fine-tune smaller LLMs with their kind of use case specific data so that they can get tool calling quality to go up

takeaways.what_they_do: A small LLM handles immediate interaction and emits one structured escalation/tool call to a larger model that has better instructions, tools, and guardrails.
Set explicit latency/cost SLAs per pipeline component, instrument each component, and scale them independently.
takeaways.evidence_quote: clear sort of guidelines and SLAs on... how much budget... independently scaling them

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep model inference and the orchestrator in the same datacenter/region to cut network hops; the speaker cites 75ms→5ms as a 30% reduction in an optimized voice setup.
takeaways.evidence_quote: drop from 75 milliseconds to five basically gets you a 30% reduction
takeaways.numbers: 75ms to 5ms network latency; ~30% reduction in optimized voice agent

takeaways.what_they_do: Scale up aggressively, but scale down by waiting for stateful long-lived sessions to finish rather than killing pods arbitrarily.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can't just arbitrarily kill a pod. You might want to wait for conversations to kind of fully finish.
